definition: Terminal User Interface; text UI rendered in a terminal.
contrast: Different from a CLI and from the running model.

definition: Command-line interface; commands and flags invoked from a shell.
contrast: A CLI command may launch a TUI or call an API.

definition: Integrated development environment, commonly editor plus debugging/build tools.
contrast: A coding agent may integrate into an IDE but run elsewhere.

definition: Goal-directed process that uses a model and may choose tools or next actions.
contrast: Not the same as the underlying model.

definition: Surrounding execution/control system for tasks, tools, permissions, state and verification.
contrast: More than a prompt and often separate from the model.

definition: Rules coordinating steps, tools, models, data and approvals.
contrast: May be fixed workflow or dynamic agent control.

definition: Long-running service exposing a model inference interface.
contrast: Serving is not identical to the model weights.

definition: Contract for sending inputs and receiving model outputs.
contrast: Can be remote or loopback.

definition: Software managing execution; always specify OS, language or inference runtime.
contrast: Not necessarily an operating system kernel.

definition: Privileged core of operating system managing processes and devices.
contrast: Different from GPU compute or notebook kernels.

definition: Program/operation executed on GPU for tensor compute.
contrast: Different from the OS kernel.

definition: Interpreter process executing notebook cells.
contrast: Not the operating system kernel.

definition: Hardware such as GPU/NPU for compute workloads.
contrast: Supported kernels and software determine usable performance.

definition: Logic directing state, policies, scheduling, authorization and actions.
contrast: Distinct from numerical compute plane.

definition: Layer executing the tensor operations needed for generation.
contrast: Does not authorize filesystem actions.

definition: Learned numerical parameters in a model.
contrast: Not an executable agent.

definition: Algorithm mapping text and control sequences to model token IDs.
contrast: Must be compatible with model embeddings.

definition: Discrete vocabulary index consumed by an embedding table.
contrast: Not always one whole word.

definition: Dense vector representation of a token or text.
contrast: Token embeddings and retrieval embeddings serve different roles.

definition: Neural architecture with attention-based sequence processing.
contrast: Model family, not an execution harness.

definition: Mechanism combining sequence-position representations.
contrast: Not a guarantee of perfect recall.

definition: Raw next-token scores before probability conversion.
contrast: Not calibrated factual confidence.

definition: Decoding control that changes distribution sharpness.
contrast: Not a factuality guarantee.

definition: Sampling filter that selects a probability-mass candidate set.
contrast: Different from top-k selection.

definition: Serialization of roles, message boundaries and tool conventions.
contrast: Not interchangeable across arbitrary models.

definition: Maximum model-visible token budget for an inference request.
contrast: Maximum size is not same as effective evidence use.

definition: High-priority model-facing instruction role where supported.
contrast: Model instruction does not grant executor permissions.

definition: Information returned by an invoked tool.
contrast: Lower-trust data, not policy authority.

definition: Initial prompt processing phase that creates attention state.
contrast: Affects time to first token.

definition: Autoregressive generation of successive output tokens.
contrast: Often memory-bandwidth sensitive.

definition: Stored attention key/value tensors from earlier token positions.
contrast: Grows with context and concurrent sequences.

definition: Grouped-query attention using fewer key/value heads.
contrast: Can reduce KV cache size.

definition: Representing tensors at reduced numerical precision.
contrast: Can change quality, speed and compatibility.

definition: Serving scheduler mixes active decoding sequences over time.
contrast: Can improve throughput with latency trade-offs.

definition: Time to first token including queueing/prefill.
contrast: Different from output tokens per second.

definition: Completed work per unit time, e.g. tokens/second.
contrast: Not the same as tail latency.

definition: Backend loading model assets and executing generation.
contrast: Distinct from HTTP serving wrapper.

definition: API, scheduling, rate limiting and operational interface over inference.
contrast: May be a separate process or integrated.

definition: Network address/route accepting structured requests.
contrast: Localhost does not mean unrestricted public access.

definition: Small automated check of process/request readiness.
contrast: Process health does not prove task correctness.

definition: Software interfacing with hardware devices.
contrast: Version compatibility matters for compute kernels.

definition: Return to a previously verified state after regression.
contrast: Must include artifacts, config and evidence.

definition: Deterministic check that output or arguments meet an explicit contract.
contrast: Not the same as asking the model to “use JSON”.

definition: Reuse of compatible identical prompt-prefix computation.
contrast: Depends on backend and isolation policy.

definition: Record of where information or decisions originated.
contrast: Necessary to trust citations and actions.

definition: Description and type requirements for tool inputs/outputs.
contrast: Not sufficient authorization by itself.

definition: Application coordinating MCP clients as part of its model workflow.
contrast: Host is not the MCP server.

definition: Protocol participant that communicates with an MCP server.
contrast: One host can manage multiple clients.

definition: Service exposing MCP tools, resources or prompts.
contrast: Still needs access control.

definition: MCP data surface addressable through a URI where supported.
contrast: Not necessarily an executable action.

definition: Defined interface for operations and data exchange.
contrast: Not intrinsically an agent or a TUI.

definition: Library simplifying use of an API/protocol.
contrast: SDK version may lag protocol spec.

definition: Protocol for inter-agent coordination/delegation.
contrast: Different goal from MCP tool exposure.

definition: Decision whether a principal may perform an action on a resource.
contrast: Must not be delegated to model text.

definition: Pattern alternating action selection and tool observations.
contrast: Does not guarantee safe actions.

definition: Pattern separating planning from execution and optional verification.
contrast: Adds orchestration overhead.

definition: Property where repeating an operation causes no additional unintended effect.
contrast: Important after timeouts.

definition: A workflow that requests human oversight at selected gates.
contrast: Must gate the executor before the action.

definition: Saved state used for resuming, reviewing or restoring a task.
contrast: Not only a chat message.

definition: Retrieval-augmented generation; supplying retrieved evidence at inference time.
contrast: Does not modify model weights.

definition: Nearest-vector retrieval using semantic representations.
contrast: Exact identifiers may need lexical search.

definition: Combination of lexical and semantic retrieval.
contrast: Often useful for code and error strings.

definition: Splitting documents into indexable text units.
contrast: Impacts recall and context.

definition: Rescoring retrieved candidates for query relevance.
contrast: Adds latency but can improve precision.

definition: Share of labeled relevant items found in top-k retrieval.
contrast: Not overall answer correctness.

definition: Checking that answer claims are supported by named source spans.
contrast: Generated citations can be incorrect.

definition: Explicit, persistent information available across task sessions.
contrast: Distinct from transient context and KV cache.

definition: System running reproducible tests and scoring outputs.
contrast: Separate from the task-execution harness.

definition: Test detecting a change from previously accepted behavior.
contrast: Must include negative and slice cases.

definition: Untrusted content attempting to change model/agent instructions.
contrast: Privilege boundaries must withstand it.

definition: Restricted execution environment limiting process capabilities.
contrast: Not a synonym for correct authorization.

definition: Grant only permissions needed for the task.
contrast: Lowers damage from mistakes/injections.

definition: Blocking check before performing a sensitive action.
contrast: Prompt-based permission is insufficient.

definition: Correlated evidence of decisions, calls, validations and outcomes.
contrast: Protect sensitive values from logging.

definition: Map assets, attackers, entry points, trust boundaries and mitigations.
contrast: Specific to actual workflow and capability.

definition: Service-level objective: measurable reliability/latency target.
contrast: Defined using SLIs and a time window.

definition: Service-level indicator measuring observed system behavior.
contrast: Needs clear instrumentation and thresholds.

definition: Latency that 95 percent of measured requests meet or beat.
contrast: Captures tail behavior better than only mean.

definition: Permitted unreliability under an agreed service objective.
contrast: Requires a meaningful SLO.

definition: Architecture decision record of options, evidence, decision and trade-offs.
contrast: Not a promotional comparison.

definition: Limited rollout used to evaluate changes before broad exposure.
contrast: Needs measurement and rollback plan.

definition: Ability to infer internal state from metrics, logs and traces.
contrast: Do not confuse with collecting everything.

definition: Single model call for a straightforward answer without external tools.
contrast: Not a guaranteed grounded workflow.

definition: Model-generated typed fields followed by external validation.
contrast: Schema validity does not prove source truth.

definition: Logic selecting one predefined branch or capability based on input.
contrast: Wrong classification can propagate errors.

definition: Deterministic ordered steps with explicit gates.
contrast: Less autonomous than agent-led tool choice.

definition: Split independent subtasks, execute concurrently, merge evidence.
contrast: Parallel calls need not be autonomous agents.

definition: Model-tool-observe loop constrained by permissions and budgets.
contrast: Open-ended autonomy adds variance and risk.

definition: Manager coordinates narrower specialist processes and reviews outputs.
contrast: Can add coordination cost and trust boundaries.

definition: Queued tasks with checkpoints, retries and idempotency controls.
contrast: Requires explicit state beyond model context.

definition: Transfer of task ownership from one agent to another.
contrast: Can lose context or approval scope.

definition: A manager treats a specialist agent as a bounded capability.
contrast: Keep nested budgets and evidence.

definition: Secondary checking stage assessing an output before an effect.
contrast: Second opinions may share correlated errors.

definition: Retry after meaningful error or feedback rather than model self-confirmation.
contrast: Must not become unbounded self-review.

definition: Forecast workload, concurrency, resource usage and limits before deployment.
contrast: Must use real workload and quality targets.

definition: Training additional updates to model parameters using task-specific data.
contrast: Different from retrieval and prompt changes.

definition: Plausible generated content unsupported or contradicted by evidence.
contrast: Requires grounding and independent checks.

definition: Stored weights, architecture metadata and compatible supporting assets.
contrast: Not identical to an inference server.

definition: Explicit criterion to stop, fail or escalate a task loop.
contrast: Independent of model requests to continue.
